To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of 3D groundwater modeling can be used to predict the transport of agrochemicals through the vadose zone to groundwater.
the transport of agricultural chemical through the soil profile is controlled by the soil texture, the soil organic matter content, and the chemical properties of the chemical.

the following factors are important in determining the transport of pesticides to ground water: (1) The soil texture of the vadose zone, (2) The depth of the water table, (3) The type of crop grown, and (4) The rate of pesticide application.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the movement of pesticides and other agrochemicals from the land surface to groundwater in coastal plain environments.
understanding the processes that control the transport of pesticides from the surface to groundwater.
understanding and predicting the fate of pesticides and other agrochemicals applied to agricultural soils and their transport through the soil to groundwater and surface water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transport of agrichemical from the surface to groundwater is a complex process that is influenced by the agrichemical, the soil, the hydrologic regime, the climate, and the management of the soil.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, as a general rule, herbicides are not transported to the groundwater through the soil profile in significant amounts.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of using the 1-D transport models to simulate the transport of pesticides and their transformation products in a coastal plain soil.
we have demonstrated that the use of 15 N as a tracer for pesticide movement is a valuable and useful tool in determining the movement and fate of pesticides in soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of agricultural chemicals can lead to groundwater contamination.
the use of pesticides and other agrochemicals is not as safe as it is often made out to be.
the transport of agrochemicals through coastal plain soils is highly variable, even at the scale of 1–ha fields.
